method: Same reconciliation as soak-2's reader_onset_rows-2.json, generalized from 4 to 9 writer lives. compactions.jsonl's t_start/t_end are NOT epoch and NOT ts_start/ts_end (D-091 not present in this build), so this run's reconciliation -- like soak2's -- goes through metrics.jsonl's compactions_total counter instead of the log's own timestamps: (a) split compactions.jsonl into its 9 writer-life segments at the 8 points where 'batches' resets to a smaller value (line boundaries recorded in life_segments); (b) within a life, compactions_total resets to 0 at writer start and its k-th increment corresponds exactly to the k-th line written to compactions.jsonl in that life (same in-process counter, same code path, confirmed here by the final compactions_total sample in each life window matching that life's own compactions.jsonl line count exactly -- see life_segments[*].final_compactions_total_in_window vs .compactions); (c) for compaction k, assign it the epoch timestamp of the first metrics.jsonl flush at which that life's compactions_total series reaches >= k (an upper bound; the previous flush is the lower bound); (d) for a target reader-onset epoch T (=run_started_epoch + onset_t_plus_s, read directly from reader-<idx>-progress.json's first_seen_ts, no clock conversion needed since it is already epoch time, unlike soak2's onset_t_plus_s which had to be converted from an elapsed-seconds field), report the largest-index compaction whose assigned upper bound is <= T as 'last compaction before T' (a conservative, guaranteed-correct choice); any further compactions whose assigned upper bound falls in the same flush bracket as T cannot be ordered against it and are reported in ambiguous_range instead of being guessed.
